cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: the next coupon date after settlement, semiannual
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as the date 15-May-11. The function is documented to return "a number that represents the next coupon date", and 2011-05-15 is serial 40678 in the 1900 date system (days since the 1899-12-30 epoch, confirmed by Python date arithmetic). Setup serials are the dates Microsoft's page prints: 40568 = 2011-01-25 (settlement), 40862 = 2011-11-15 (maturity), frequency 2 (semiannual), basis 1 (actual/actual). Counting coupon dates back from maturity in six-month steps gives 2011-11-15, 2011-05-15, 2010-11-15, so the settlement date falls in the coupon period 2010-11-15 to 2011-05-15, so the next coupon after 2011-01-25 is 2011-05-15

cases.description: The same bond paying annually instead of semiannually
cases.expected_note: With frequency 1 the coupon dates are 2011-11-15 and 2010-11-15, so the next coupon after the 2011-01-25 settlement is 2011-11-15 = serial 40862 -- which for this bond coincides with the maturity date. This discriminates the frequency argument, which the documented example alone does not

cases.description: A frequency of 3, which is not one of the permitted values
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If frequency is any number other than 1, 2, or 4, COUPNCD returns the #NUM! error value."

cases.description: A day-count basis of 5, above the documented maximum of 4
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If basis < 0 or if basis > 4, COUPNCD returns the #NUM! error value."

cases.description: Settlement and maturity swapped, so settlement is after maturity
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If settlement >= maturity, COUPNCD returns the #NUM! error value."
